findings.title: deleteCache ownership check fails for delegated credentials
findings.body: The handler authorizes the request with `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. Delegation credentials often have `userId: null` (or an in-memory/negative id), so a user whose Google calendar is connected via a DelegationCredential will always get 'Credential not found or access denied' even though the UI (CredentialActionsDropdown) shows the 'Delete cached data' action for those credentials (hasCache is true when delegationCredentialId is set and canDisconnect is false). The user will always see 'Error deleting cache'. The check needs to account for delegated-to credentials the user has access to, or the UI must hide the delete action for them.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: After successfully deleting the cache via `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache`, the component only calls `onSuccess?.()`. Unlike the disconnect mutation (which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in onSettled), the delete-cache path never invalidates the `connectedCalendars` query. In the web wrapper `onChanged` is often undefined, so the UI will keep showing the old 'Cache Status / Last updated' timestamp (and the delete option) until an unrelated refetch happens, making the user think deletion didn't work.

findings.title: Timestamp hardcoded to en-US and ignores user locale
findings.body: The cache 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` instead of using the user's locale from `useLocale()`. All non-US users will see US-formatted dates (MM/DD/YYYY, 12-hour clock), inconsistent with the rest of the localized UI.

findings.title: Nested interactive elements / non-interactive DropdownMenuItem
findings.body: `DropdownItem` (renders a `<button>`) is nested inside `DropdownMenuItem`, which itself renders a menu item element — this produces invalid nested interactive DOM and can break keyboard navigation and screen readers. The cache-status block is also rendered as a selectable menu item (line 84) that does nothing when clicked/activated, which is confusing for keyboard users; it should be a non-interactive label.

findings.title: Deleting the cache does not repopulate it while webhooks remain active
findings.body: `deleteCacheHandler` deletes all CalendarCache rows for the credential but leaves the Google webhook channel subscriptions intact and never triggers `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`. The cache is only repopulated on webhook events (which only fire on actual calendar changes) or the unwatch flow. For organizations relying on the calendar-cache feature, this means after deletion every availability check falls back to live Google freebusy API calls indefinitely until some calendar change occurs, defeating the purpose of the cache and risking Google API quota exhaustion. Deletion should trigger a re-fetch (as `unwatchCalendar` does with `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`).

findings.title: Authorization failure thrown as generic Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential isn't found/owned, the handler throws a plain `Error('Credential not found or access denied')`, which tRPC surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) with the message leaking to the client. Cal.com's convention is to throw `TRPCError({ code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' | 'NOT_FOUND' })` so clients get correct status codes and no server error noise/alerting.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object is opaque and fragile
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` relies on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` bump when `data` is empty to work at all. This is undocumented/fragile behavior (some Prisma versions reject empty update data), updates rows even when the preceding cache writes failed, and communicates no intent. It also clobbers nothing but bumps `updatedAt` for all selected calendars of the credential, which the PR description itself flags as unused by the frontend — either give it an explicit data payload or remove the call until the field is consumed.

findings.title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and fails on Linux
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "..." "$ENV_FILE"`. On GNU/Linux sed, `-i ''` is interpreted as an empty file operand and the command fails, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated on Linux dev machines. Also the relative `ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on the caller's cwd. Use a portable check (e.g. `sed -i.bak`) or detect the platform.

findings.title: No tests for new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds or deleteCache handler
findings.body: The PR adds a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, including the groupBy/_max mapping and null handling), a new tRPC mutation (`deleteCache`), and new enrichment logic in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, but includes no unit or e2e tests for any of them. In particular the credential-ownership check and the empty-credentialIds edge case are untested.
